local_review.finding_body: `tests/src/org.bytedeco/tesseract/5.5.1-1.5.12/build.gradle` hardcoded `org.bytedeco:tesseract-platform:5.5.1-1.5.12`. That made the suite use 5.5.1 native binaries when the harness tests another Tesseract version, violating the version-agnostic test requirement in §FS-test-contract.2.5.
local_review.fix_note: Changed the companion `tesseract-platform` runtime dependency to use the harness-provided `$libraryVersion`, matching the tested Tesseract artifact and existing JavaCPP platform-test practice. The exact Forge finalization command then passed cleanly.
local_review.review_comment: Approved after repair. I verified the diff is limited to one new coordinate and its metadata, index, stats, and test project; the tests are library-specific public-API tests in a separate package, contain no scaffold, native-image skip or tolerated failure, prohibited build flag, visibility bypass, reflection shortcut, or legacy metadata format. The resolved 0/0 dynamic-access result is a valid no-calls case, so the percentage and entry-count mismatch gates do not apply. Local index gates were green, and the exact Forge finalization command completed successfully across all three native lanes, metadata validation, style checks, generated-test checks, and regenerated statistics without a further publishable change.
